summary: Critical emergency contacts for Kenya, including Nairobi and Mombasa. Kenya has the strongest private hospital infrastructure in East Africa. Know these numbers before you need them.

police.description: Kenya National Police Service emergency line
police.notes: Also reachable at 112 from mobile. The DCI (Directorate of Criminal Investigations) for non-emergency crime reporting: +254 20 4341234.

ambulance.notes: Kenya Red Cross ambulance: +254 703 037000. St. John Ambulance Kenya: +254 20 2210000. Private ambulance services (AMREF, Nairobi Hospital) are often faster in urban areas.

fire.notes: Nairobi County Fire: +254 20 2222181. Response times outside Nairobi and Mombasa can be very slow.

tourist.notes: Specifically for crimes against tourists and visitor assistance. Available during business hours.

embassies.name: U.S. Embassy Nairobi
embassies.emergencyNote: Call main number after hours and select the emergency option for U.S. citizen services

embassies.name: British High Commission Nairobi
embassies.emergencyNote: Call main number after hours for the out-of-hours emergency recording and duty officer

embassies.name: Canadian High Commission Nairobi
embassies.emergencyNote: Ottawa Emergency Watch and Response Centre for after-hours citizen emergencies

hospitals.name: Aga Khan University Hospital
hospitals.notes: East Africa's premier private hospital. Full emergency and trauma center, ICU, specialist services. Accepts major international insurance. Preferred by expats and diplomatic community.

hospitals.name: Nairobi Hospital
hospitals.notes: Full-service private hospital with strong emergency department. Has its own ambulance service. Accepts international insurance. Well-regarded for cardiac and orthopedic care.

hospitals.name: Kenyatta National Hospital
hospitals.notes: Kenya's national referral hospital. Largest in East Africa. Best for serious trauma when private options are not accessible. Can be crowded and under-resourced.

hospitals.name: Coast General Teaching and Referral Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital for the coast region. Referral destination for serious emergencies in Mombasa and surrounding counties.

insurance.nhis: Kenya's National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) covers Kenyan citizens and some residents. Visitors should carry comprehensive travel insurance. NHIF is not applicable to tourists.
insurance.recommendation: Carry travel insurance that explicitly covers medical evacuation. Aga Khan and Nairobi Hospital are world-class but serious long-term care may require evacuation to South Africa or Europe. AMREF Flying Doctors offers annual evacuation memberships popular with expats.

keyAlerts: Dial 999 or 112 (mobile) for all emergencies: police, fire, ambulance
Aga Khan Hospital in Nairobi is the gold standard for private emergency care in East Africa
AMREF Flying Doctors provides medical evacuation across the continent. Worth an annual membership if staying long-term
Mombasa has significantly fewer private hospital options than Nairobi. Plan accordingly for coastal visits
The Kenya Tourist Police Unit (+254 20 2888022) is specifically for crimes against visitors
